newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end sharply lower on trade, Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end sharply lower on trade, Wall St.

text.p: Brazilian shares dropped 4.76 percent Friday on a larger-than-expected July trade gap, a drop in U.S. stocks and concerns the Central Bank may shut down several brokerages next week, dealers said.
"When you begin accummulating all this, people get nervous. They don't know where the market's going," a dealer at local Cresiful brokerage said.
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index .BVSP of 47 most-trade issues fell 613 points to end at 12,259 points on moderately weak volume of 823.8 million reais ($760.1 million).
Brokers said the market began tumbling early in the session, first on concerns about a larger-than-expected July trade gap and later fueled by sharp declines on Wall Street.

But stocks dropped more in early afternoon when confirmation came that Brazil was likely to post a $811 million July trade deficit. Economists had expected a $570 million gap, according to the latest Reuters poll BRAAL.
Finally, a report the government plans to release a list of brokerages it plans to close next week after a Central Bank investigation sent further jitters through the bolsa.
"This has people nervous," one broker said.
The bolsa's benchmark issue, Telebras preferred, was among the major losers, retreating 5.59 percent to end at 152 reais. The share accounted for 60 percent of total trade.
Other leading blue chips also plummeted. Federal power holding Eletrobras dropped 6.25 percent to end at 600 reais while its common closed off 6.26 percent at 553.01 reais.
But the drop in the Bovespa was virtually across the board, and included even steep falls among second- and third-tier issues.

Power sector stocks, which rallied Thursday on the sale of Bahia state utility Coelba despite a broader market drop, also fell Friday with the bolsa's Electrical Energy Index .IEE sliding 3.93 percent to end at 3,485 points.
Brokers said the market closed amid nervous trading and was likely to open in the same mood Monday, anxious to hear the results of the Central Bank's probe.
